method: Each of the six existing full-page PNGs was opened exactly once in capture order. Observations below describe visible layout and notation rendering, not mathematical correctness. Recorded DOM and font metrics supplement, but do not replace, those pixel observations.
limitations: Long full-page images were inspected in the tool's single display. No crop, second opening, or independent magnified raster was made. This is not a claim of glyph-by-glyph pixel metrology.

The DOM rectangles are the saved pre-screenshot browser observations. Full-page capture can present a slightly different scrollbar/reflow state; exact screenshot cutoff coordinates are not inferred from DOM coordinates alone.
Native-radio action assertions were recorded before navigation reset. The screenshots intentionally show the subsequent unselected view, not answer-key selections.
The narrow KaTeX subscript wrappers have unusual line boxes and approximately 2px scroll-width differences. These measurements alone do not establish wrong font size or missing painted glyphs.

observations: The title, all text sections and bottom writing-exercise jump are present in the full-page view. The centered reading column has clear margins and no visible adjacent-paragraph collision.

Fractions, decimal points, ellipses, minus signs, comparison signs and the integer-only bars over 2, 1 and 118 are visibly rendered. The long -117 mixed-number chain fits this desktop view, including its final decimal tail.

The a_0, a_k and b_0 subscripts flagged by tiny native scroll-width discrepancies are visibly legible. No corresponding missing painted subscript was established in this opening; the original DOM failure is preserved.
The final zero-tail convention paragraphs, comparison formula, barred-1 comparison example and bottom note remain visible. This is a rendering observation only.
Exercise numbers 113 and 114, six and four subpart labels respectively, and the return link fit in the single desktop viewport. Numbers and body text are separated.
All visible fractions, negative signs, decimal strings and the final 114d ellipsis are readable without an observed missing mathematical token. No repeated-4 count or mathematical answer is inferred.
113d, 113e and 113f show short gray vertical scrollbar thumbs beside the fraction wrappers. These are actual screenshot artifacts, not answer inputs; they are recorded as F002.
The existing writing page has no answer-input controls. No missing interactive writing widget is invented for this offline view.
Questions 1 through 10, all A-D or A-C option rows, and the bottom return link are visible across the full-page image. No right-edge option is cut off.
Radio circles, option letters and option text use separate columns. Wrapped option 2B and the longer question stems preserve clear separation from following options.
The fraction stems, a_0 subscripts, negative signs, comparison signs, decimal tails and integer-bar notations in questions 3, 5 and 6 are visible. Bars do not visually span entire decimal strings.
Questions 7 through 10 and their final options remain fully present. All 38 option layouts were inspected for presentation, without choosing or validating their correct answers.

The title metadata wraps to a second line; all text sections and the bottom exercise jump remain present. Ordinary text, the shorter formulas and the final note wrap without observed adjacent-paragraph collision.

The long chain beginning with -117 and a stacked 1/3 fraction is a single horizontal line. Its final barred-118 decimal tail is visibly cut off at the right in the default full-page image; only the beginning of that last decimal segment is visible. F001 is a real default-view detail loss.

The saved browser data show that this wrapper can be scrolled internally to its far right. That accessibility does not make all mathematical details visible simultaneously and does not cure the default screenshot failure.
The shorter barred-2, barred-1 and final comparison examples remain legible. Tiny a_0, a_k and b_0 internal-box discrepancies do not independently establish a painted-glyph defect.
Both exercise numbers, all six 113 subparts, all four 114 subparts and the return link fit in the 390x844 image. The rightmost 114 decimal comparison and its terminal punctuation are present.

Exercise numbers do not collide with the subpart text. Fractions, decimal points, minus signs and the visible repeated-4 ellipsis remain readable; no semantic judgment or source-count reconstruction is made.
The same gray scrollbar thumbs appear next to the 113d/e/f fractions. F002 applies to both viewports and is not excused by the native horizontal-overflow checks passing.
All ten questions and all 38 option rows appear in the long mobile view, including question 10D and the bottom return link.
Options in questions 1 and 2 break into multiple lines. The explanatory and notation-heavy rows in 3, 5 and 6 also wrap; radio circles and letters stay separate from the wrapped text.

Fractions, a_0 subscripts, decimal ellipses, signs and integer bars remain visible. The comparison alternatives in questions 7 through 10 fit their columns without an observed missing rightmost or bottom token.

No radio/letter/text collision, option-over-option collision or hidden last option was observed. The long image's single display is combined with the captured per-option geometry and all 38 native label-selection assertions; it is not a mathematical review.

findings.title: Mobile default view clips the final decimal tail of a long body equation
findings.selector: p.para at captured zero-based index 11; descendant .nb whose KaTeX annotation is the bound -117 equation
findings.impact: The page-level overflow assertion passes, but the default formula view omits the end of the decimal expansion. The requirement that all mathematical details be visible is not met.
findings.minimal_recommendation_not_applied: In a separately authorized repair, allow this equality chain to break at equality boundaries or supply a deliberate fully visible multiline formula layout, preserving every token and the integer-only overline scope. Do not alter the mathematics or force a smaller-than-contract font to conceal the problem.

findings.title: Unexpected native scrollbar thumbs beside short writing-exercise fractions
findings.observed: Short gray vertical scrollbar thumbs are visibly adjacent to 1/4, -1/4 and -2/3. All mathematical tokens remain readable in this batch, and no collision or glyph loss is established.
findings.cause_status: The overflow wrapper is a candidate cause, not a proven vertical-metric diagnosis; overflow-y and vertical scroll dimensions were not captured. No extra browser check was run.
findings.minimal_recommendation_not_applied: Review short inline-math overflow containment in a separately authorized repair. Preserve fractions, signs, baseline, KaTeX_Main sizing and punctuation; do not hide a scrollbar by clipping actual mathematical ink.

native_failure_adjudication.desktop_text_tiny_width_flags: No corresponding painted-glyph clipping was established in the single screenshot opening. They are recorded as unconfirmed internal-geometry warnings, not a font/em defect.
native_failure_adjudication.mobile_text_long_chain: Both saved geometry and the single screenshot opening establish a real default-view failure.
native_failure_adjudication.writing_views: Native DOM checks passed, but actual screenshots add the nonblocking scrollbar finding F002.
